source.title: Time Commitment Grant Proposal — Python interface documentation + automated testing for FreeCAD
source.body:
**Grant type:** Time Commitment
**Proposed project:** Python interface documentation + automated testing for FreeCAD

### Proposal description
I propose an hours-based engagement improving two maintainability surfaces of FreeCAD that are written in Python: the Python API documentation for Python-backed subsystems, and automated unit/regression test coverage for the same layer, prioritized by FreeCAD maintainers at kickoff. This benefits FreeCAD users and developers with accurate, current API docs; contributors with meaningful regression signal; and the release cycle — testing and documentation are explicitly the 2026 FreeCAD grant priorities. I have never worked on FreeCAD before — rather than pretend expertise in CAD internals, I propose a plan whose first milestone is a public, verifiable audit that proves my ability to deliver without close mentorship.

### Deliverables
- **D1 (Week 1): Public audit.** A documented audit of FreeCAD's Python-facing surface — stale API references, dead documentation links, Python workbenches with zero or broken unit tests, and missing release-cycle smoke coverage — filed as an issue thread in the FreeCAD repository, every finding linked. Deliverable is the audit itself plus an agreed priority list picked *by maintainers*, so the remaining work targets what they actually want.
- **D2 (Weeks 2–4): Documentation fixes.** At least 6 PRs merged (or review-ready) addressing the prioritized documentation defects — stale pages, dead links, missing Python API coverage — following FreeCAD's own documentation conventions, with before/after evidence attached per PR.
- **D3 (Weeks 5–8): Testing.** An automated regression/unit test suite (or extensions to the existing one — whichever FreeCAD maintainers prefer) for one Python-backed workbench named at kickoff, with ≥20 new tests, all green in CI, plus a release-cycle smoke-test checklist.
- **D4 (Ongoing): Weekly status notes** posted to the FreeCAD forum thread tied to this grant, so the FPA and community can see progress at all times.

### Timeline
- **Can start:** immediately upon grant approval and kickoff call.
- **Time available:** ~20 hours/week, for **8 weeks** (~160 hours).
- **First week** is onboarding + the D1 audit — deliberately before any code or docs are touched.

### Risks and mitigation
- *Risk:* No prior FreeCAD internals exposure. *Mitigation:* D1 is a bounded audit with no deliverable dependent on CAD knowledge; maintainers act on audit findings, which keeps every later step aimed at real need; if the first week shows I cannot deliver, maintainers see that before anything else is paid.
- *Risk:* Documentation priorities may differ from my guesses. *Mitigation:* D1 exists so the priorities are theirs, not mine; I shift D2–D3 per their kickoff feedback.
- *Risk:* Availability drops mid-project. *Mitigation:* 20 h/week is committed conservatively; weekly forum updates mean any gap surfaces early; I can pause and FPA may adjust scope rather than silently sink hours into something doomed.

### Compensation
- **Per-hour rate:** **EUR 25/hour** (≈ USD 27/hour), local currency EUR.
- **Estimated total:** ~160 hours over 8 weeks ≈ **EUR 4,000** (upper bound; I will only bill hours actually worked).
- Happy to adjust rate inside the 20–35 EUR/h range on FPA's request, provided the plan stays fixed-goal internally.

### About you
- **Name:** Lee Muriithi Kingori
- **Forum / Community username(s):** GitHub: `leettlest`
- **Experience relevant to the proposal:** Python automation and developer tooling. Most recently, an offline Click CliRunner test suite covering every command of an open-source Python SDK (rustchain-bounties #17181, PR: Scottcjn/Rustchain#8686), which exercises the same discipline this grant needs: accurate docs, regression-first testing, CI-green PRs.
- **Have you contributed to FreeCAD before?** No — this is a deliberate first contribution, structured so my first paid deliverable does not claim knowledge I do not have.
- **Have you worked on similar software before?** Yes — source-available Python projects with public test/CI standards (CLI SDKs, automation frameworks).
- **Have you solved similar tasks before?** Yes — audit-driven fixes: audit, file findings, land PRs in priority order, with links to each change.

### Verification / process
Once approved, I will open a weekly progress thread on the FreeCAD forum, and keep all work as public PRs/issues on FreeCAD repositories so the FPA can review at any time. I understand payment (if any) follows FPA's standard contract, stage by stage.
